header.sector: AI accelerators, GPUs, custom silicon and their direct supply chain
header.title: Huawei-DeepSeek co-design matures a domestic Chinese AI compute ecosystem

s01_bottom_line.text: DeepSeek released Ascend support for six software repositories, and SemiAnalysis documents via microbenchmarks that the Huawei Ascend ecosystem is maturing through co-design with DeepSeek, with software at the frontier even as hardware lags Nvidia. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩

The article argues Huawei's ecosystem is already mature and that DeepSeek will likely primarily use Huawei's stack by 2027-2028 under pressure to build a fully domestic Chinese ecosystem. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

A maturing Huawei-DeepSeek domestic stack could shift Chinese AI compute demand toward Ascend and away from Nvidia over time, but the article does not quantify any earnings, revenue or market-share effect for listed suppliers.

items.text: Huawei's best stock kernels reach 99.7% of the compute ceiling on BF16 GEMM shapes.
TileLang AutoSchedule reduces single-operation execution time by up to 40% on 950PR, especially for smaller sizes.
DeepSeek released Ascend support for six repositories before China's national day holidays.
DeepSeek will likely be primarily using Huawei's stack by 2027 or 2028. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Pointer-chase latency stays near 134ns through 18 blocks, rises to 182ns at 56 blocks, then jumps to 391ns at 64 — consistent with a second wave beyond 56 Vector cores. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
This 950PR SKU has 7 configured, 6 visible, and 5 executing AICPU cores.

s03_transmission.text: DeepSeek and Huawei co-design hardware and software, releasing Ascend support for key repositories, narrowing the software ecosystem gap with Nvidia.
If DeepSeek shifts primarily to Huawei's stack, Ascend accelerator volumes in China would rise at Nvidia's expense, though the article does not quantify this. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Increased Ascend adoption would benefit Huawei (private) and its domestic supply chain, but no listed-company earnings effect is quantified.

qualifiers: driven by external and internal pressure to build a fully domestic Chinese ecosystem
s04_key_evidence.quote: In 2028 or even 2027, DeepSeek will likely be primarily using Huawei’s stack

s04_key_evidence.label: DeepSeek provides Huawei with model weights, supporting Day-0 optimized releases such as DeepSeek V4 and V4.1.
s04_key_evidence.quote: DeepSeek provides Huawei with weights, supporting Day-0 optimized releases, such as DeepSeek V4 and V4.1

s04_key_evidence.label: HBM bandwidth utilization
s04_key_evidence.quote: 950PR’s effective bandwidth and bandwidth utilization surpassing H100 at small message size per buffers, and nearly matching H100 in bandwidth utilization at large message sizes

s04_key_evidence.label: Huawei's architecture is reshaping DeepSeek's software: the new FlashMLA KV-cache layout co-locates quantized values and scales to cut MTE transfer requests on Ascend.
s04_key_evidence.quote: The new implementation places them together, reducing the number of transfer requests by the memory transfer engine(MTE).

s04_key_evidence.label: The 950PR's Linx816 AArch64 AICPU cores are likely the same as the middle cores in Huawei's Kirin 9000S/9010 SoCs.
s04_key_evidence.quote: these cores are likely the same as the middle cores in the Kirin 9000S/9010

s04_key_evidence.label: Huawei provides hardware and software stack while DeepSeek provides workloads and engineering, a symbiotic exchange.
s04_key_evidence.quote: Huawei provides the hardware and native software stack; DeepSeek brings the workloads and engineering needed to make that hardware useful for its models

s04_key_evidence.label: Huawei has joined NVIDIA in commercializing large scale-up AI systems via Ascend supernodes spanning multiple racks.
s04_key_evidence.quote: Huawei has joined NVIDIA in commercializing large scale-up AI systems, with its Ascend supernodes extending tightly coupled accelerator interconnects across multiple racks

s04_key_evidence.label: DeepSeek released Ascend support for six repositories before China's national day holidays.
s04_key_evidence.quote: DeepSeek released Ascend support for TileLang , DeepGEMM , DeepEP , TileKernels , FlashMLA , and DeepSelect

s04_key_evidence.label: The Ascend 950 backend is merged into the main TileLang repository rather than only a separate Huawei adapter, adding native compilation, scheduling and runtime integration.
s04_key_evidence.quote: Ascend 950 backend is merged into the main TileLang repository, rather than existing only in a separate Huawei adapter.

s04_key_evidence.label: The Ascend 950PR is designed for prefill and recommendation and has lower memory bandwidth and core count than the larger 950DT.
s04_key_evidence.quote: Ascend 950PR is designed for prefill and recommendation. It gets lower memory bandwidth and core than its bigger brother the 950DT.

s04_key_evidence.label: Huawei's Kimi K3 recipe explicitly restricts vector use to leave capacity for concurrent work, illustrating the resource-balancing co-design problem beyond DeepSeek.
s04_key_evidence.quote: Huawei’s Kimi K3 recipe explicitly restricts vector use to leave capacity for concurrent work

s04_key_evidence.label: Huawei's Ascend supernodes evolved from the 910 CloudMatrix384 to the 950 SuperPod, extending accelerator interconnects across multiple racks.
s04_key_evidence.quote: from the 910 CloudMatrix384 to the 950 SuperPod

s04_key_evidence.label: TileLang can match and beat CANN in certain cases, with the preferred implementation changing with size (warm-cache naive benchmark).
s04_key_evidence.quote: it can match and beat CANN at certain cases; the preferred implementation changes with size

s04_key_evidence.label: DeepEP-Ascend, proposed by Huawei's Ascend team in July 2025 but initially declined, is now distributed under DeepSeek's own organization.
s04_key_evidence.quote: In July 2025, Huawei’s Ascend team proposed DeepEP-Ascend under deepseek-ai , but a DeepEP maintainer declined . Today, DeepEP-Ascend is distributed under DeepSeek’s own organization.

s04_key_evidence.label: Performance per watt or TCO is the best chip comparison, and in China watts are far cheaper — favoring Ascend's economics despite weaker per-chip performance.
s04_key_evidence.quote: But for China, watts are far cheaper. We’ll analyze Ascend’s perf per TCO in a future article.
